## Cross-Correlation Analyses
```{r chunk05_1}
source("04_data_formatting.R")
```

### Data

We load and process the data and create our main dataframe.
```{r chunk05_2}
dat_country0  <- data.clean("multi_vaccine_indirect_postcovid19",country_index)
dat_country0 <-  dat_country0 %>%
  filter((year >= 2023 & year <= 2024))     
dat_country0 <- dat_country0[order(dat_country0$year_decimal), ]
country_name <- unique(dat_country0$country)
virus_name <- unique(dat_country0$virus)
#virus_name <- factor(virus_name, levels = c("RSV", "PIV", "HMPV", "RV","ADV", "HCoV", "HBoV"))
print(virus_name)
dat_country0 <- dat_country0[,c("country","year","month","year_decimal","date",
                                "virus","AAP","fluA_AAP", "fluB_AAP", "flu_AAP","strategy2_general_coverage",
                                "temp2m","abshum")]
colnames(dat_country0)[8:13] <- c("INF_A","INF_B","INF_ALL","Vaccine","Temp","AH")
data_country <- pivot_wider(dat_country0, names_from = virus, values_from = AAP)
data_country <- data_country[,c("country","year","month","year_decimal","date",
                        "Vaccine","Temp","AH",
                        "INF_A","INF_B","INF_ALL",virus_name)]

```

### Cross-Correlation
```{r chunk05_function}
plot.xcor <- function(x, y, mainTitle){

xcorr_x_y <- ccf(x, y, lag.max = 12, na.action=na.pass,
                            type = c("correlation", "covariance"),
                            plot = TRUE, main = "", axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
  box(col="black")
  axis(1, col="black", col.ticks="black", col.axis="black", cex.axis=1, tck = 0.02)
  mtext("Time lag (week)", side=1, line=2.2, col="black", cex=1)
  
  axis(2, col="black", col.ticks="black", col.axis="black", cex.axis=1, tck = 0.02)
  mtext(expression(paste("Cross-correlation with incidence (",rho,")")), side=2, line=2, 
        col="black", cex=0.8)
  
  # # Use logical conditions to filter values with lag greater than 0
  #bio_lag <- xcorr_x_y$lag[which(xcorr_x_y$acf == max(xcorr_x_y$acf[xcorr_x_y$lag > 0]))]
  #bio_lag <- xcorr_x_y$lag[which(xcorr_x_y$acf == max(xcorr_x_y$acf))]
  bio_lag <- xcorr_x_y$lag[which(abs(xcorr_x_y$acf) == max(abs(xcorr_x_y$acf)))]
  abline(v = bio_lag, col = '#e74c3c', lwd = 2, lty = 3)
  title(mainTitle, cex.main=1.4)
  
 # Extract lag values and corresponding correlation coefficients
  lag_acf_df <- data.frame(
    Lag = xcorr_x_y$lag,
    ACF = xcorr_x_y$acf)
    
   return(list(lag_acf_df = lag_acf_df, max_lag = bio_lag))
}

```



```{r,chunk05_virus_pair, fig.width=15, fig.height=16, dpi=300}
ccm_parameter_lag <- c()
#data_country <- data_country[,c("country","year","month","year_decimal","ISOYM",
#                                "virus","cases","INF_A","INF_B","INF_ALL")]

# Define variables for pairwise analysis
all_vars_other <- c(virus_name,"INF_A","INF_B","INF_ALL")
all_vars_flu <- c("INF_A","INF_B","INF_ALL","Vaccine","Temp","AH")

#var_pairs = combn(all_vars, 2) # Combinations of vars, 2 at a time
#colnames(var_pairs) <- paste0(var_pairs[1,],":",var_pairs[2,])
#all_vars1 <- unique(colnames(var_pairs)) 
#print(all_vars1)

# Generate pairwise variable combinations
var_pairs <- expand.grid(all_vars_flu, all_vars_other)
var_pairs$Var1 <- as.character(var_pairs$Var1)
var_pairs$Var2 <- as.character(var_pairs$Var2)

var_pairs <- var_pairs[var_pairs$Var1 != var_pairs$Var2, ]
var_pairs <- t(var_pairs)
colnames(var_pairs) <- paste0(var_pairs[1,],":",var_pairs[2,])
all_vars1 <- unique(colnames(var_pairs)) 
var_pairs <- var_pairs[, order(var_pairs[1,])]
print(var_pairs)
print(all_vars1)
```



```{r,chunk05_plot, fig.width=20, fig.height=15, dpi=300}
ccf_cor_coef <- matrix(nrow=25, ncol=ncol(var_pairs))
ccf_cor_coef <-as.data.frame(ccf_cor_coef) 
#par(mfrow = c(3, 5), mar = c(3.5,3.5,1.7,1), mgp = c(2,0.5,0), oma = c(0,0,0,0))
par(mfrow = c(6, 10), mar = c(3.5,3.5,1.7,1), mgp = c(2,0.5,0), oma = c(0,0,3,0))

for (l in 1:ncol(var_pairs)){
col_var1 <-  which(colnames(data_country) == var_pairs[1,l])
col_var2 <-   which(colnames(data_country) == var_pairs[2,l]) 
col_name <- colnames(var_pairs)[l]

# Set Var2 as x and Var1 as y, consistent with the subsequent CCM analysis
lag_var1_var2 <- plot.xcor(data_country[,col_var1], data_country[,col_var2], col_name)

## save lag
ccm_parameter_lag <-  cbind(ccm_parameter_lag,lag_var1_var2$max_lag)
colnames(ccm_parameter_lag)[l] <- paste0("lag_",colnames(var_pairs)[l])

# save correlation coefficient
ccf_lag <- lag_var1_var2$lag_acf_df["Lag"]
ccf_cor_coef[,l] <-  lag_var1_var2$lag_acf_df["ACF"]
#colnames(ccf_cor_coef)[1] <- "Lag"
colnames(ccf_cor_coef)[l] <- colnames(var_pairs)[l]
}

#plot
mtext(country_name, outer = TRUE, cex = 1.5,line=1)
output_name <- paste("02_output/01_parameter_selection/01_Cross-Correlation/", country_index, "_", country_name, sep="")
file_name = paste(output_name, ".pdf", sep="")
dev.copy(pdf, file=file_name, width = 20, height = 15)
dev.off()

#save result
print(ccm_parameter_lag)
ccf_cor_coef <- cbind(ccf_lag,ccf_cor_coef)
ccf_cor_coef$country <- country_name
print(ccf_cor_coef)
write.csv(ccf_cor_coef,paste("02_output/01_parameter_selection/01_Cross-Correlation/", country_index, "_", country_name,".csv", sep=""),row.names = F)
```
